title: That Blessed Law of Thine
description: That Blessed Law of Thine in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 229, “Desire for Holiness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: That bless-ed law of Thine, Fa-ther, to me im-part; The Spi-rit's law of life di-vine, O, write it in my heart!

lines: The Spirit's law of life divine,
O, write it in my heart!
The law of liberty from sin,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
